SK2073 The caught exception is not passed to the logger's exception parameter

An error-level logging call inside a catch clause does not give the logger the exception the clause caught, although the overload that takes one exists.

CategoryCorrectness
Default severitywarning
ScopeSemantic
Needs a compilationyes
Runs under --load=looseno
Cached per fileyes
Fixyes, safe
Language version floor—
Since2.0
SupersedesS6667, S6668

Why

Every one of these APIs takes the exception in its own parameter, and that parameter is what a sink treats as an exception: it is where the stack trace, the inner chain and the type end up as structure rather than as a sentence in a message. Left empty, the entry says something went wrong and carries nothing anybody can act on, which is the whole reason the line was written. ⚠ This is `SK7xxx` on the issue and `SK2xxx` here. An entry that cannot be diagnosed from is a defect in the program's observable behaviour rather than a maintenance cost, and the same argument that puts SK2014 — a catch that swallows without logging or rethrow — in the correctness band puts this next to it.

Example

Instead of:

catch (IOException ex) {
    logger.LogError("could not read {Path}", path);
}

Write:

catch (IOException ex) {
    logger.LogError(ex, "could not read {Path}", path);
}

When it does not fire

⚠ Error and critical levels only (LogError, LogCritical, Error, Fatal). An information- or debug-level line inside a catch is very often deliberate — an expected exception, handled, noted in passing — and reporting those is how a rule about logging becomes noise about control flow. ⚠ Nothing is reported unless the repair exists: the analysis looks up an overload with an exception parameter on the logging type first, so a logger that has none has no defect this rule can name and the fix cannot assume an overload into being. ⚠ Only the `Log*(template, values…)` shape is reported, and that is a correctness constraint rather than caution. Microsoft.Extensions.Logging orders its event-id overload (EventId, Exception, string), so an exception prepended in front of an event id does not bind — skala fix would have broken the build on the tool's own advice. A call that writes anything before the template is declined outright rather than reported with a fix that cannot be applied. ⚠ A call that already passes the exception as a *template argument* still fires, because the exception parameter is still empty and a sink still gets a string where it expected an exception; the fix attaches the exception and does not also delete the now-redundant hole, because removing text from inside a literal needs a value-to-source offset map that escape sequences break, and a fix that is right except after a \n is worse than one that leaves a tidy-up for the author. A catch with no declared variable (catch { }, catch (IOException)) has no exception to pass and is silent. The nearest enclosing catch is the one used, and the walk stops at the member declaration rather than at the first try, so a lambda or local function written inside a catch — which really does close over the variable — is still reported. Binding is by containing type (Serilog.ILogger, Serilog.Log, Microsoft.Extensions.Logging.LoggerExtensions), never by method name. Generated code is excluded.
